questions.question: In May 2025, what change did the Supreme Court make regarding environmental clearances (EC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rejected retrospective ECs as illegal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** in May 2025 ruled that granting **retrospective environmental clearances** (ECs) was **illegal** and violative of established environmental laws.
 
• Retrospective ECs refer to environmental clearances issued **after the commencement of a project**, effectively legalizing activities that were undertaken without prior approval.
 
• The court emphasized that projects must secure **environmental clearances before their initiation**, as mandated under the **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006**.
 
• This ruling was a significant step to ensure that industries and projects comply with **environmental regulations** and do not bypass mandatory procedural requirements.
 
• The decision aimed to protect the environment by ensuring that **public hearings** and **impact assessments** are conducted before the project approval process, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability in environmental governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006:**

 
 
• The EIA Notification requires projects to undergo an **environmental clearance process** before any physical activity begins.
 
• The process includes the preparation of an **EIA report**, public consultation, and appraisal by an expert committee.
 
• This notification applies to various sectors, including **industry, mining, infrastructure, and energy projects**.
 
 
 
• **Public Hearing Process:**
 
 
• A **public hearing** is conducted as part of the EIA process to ensure **community participation** in decision-making.
 
• Stakeholders, including local residents, environmental activists, and government representatives, can voice their concerns about the project.
 
• This process ensures that the social and environmental impacts of the project are adequately addressed.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Role in Environmental Governance:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has played a pivotal role in enforcing **environmental laws** and ensuring compliance with constitutional provisions like **Article 21**, which guarantees the **right to a clean and healthy environment**.
 
• Several landmark rulings, such as the **Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum vs. Union of India**, have strengthened environmental jurisprudence in India.
 
 
 
• **Illegal Retrospective Clearances:**
 
 
• Retrospective ECs allow projects to bypass mandatory processes, undermining **environmental protection frameworks**.
 
• Such clearances have often led to **environmental degradation** due to lack of proper planning and mitigation measures.
 
• The Supreme Court's ruling in May 2025 reinforces adherence to **prior approval mechanisms**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Protection Act, 1986:**

 
 
• This act forms the legal basis for environmental clearances in India.
 
• It empowers the government to take measures for protecting and improving the quality of the environment.
 
• It also provides the framework for regulating activities that impact the environment.
 
 
 
• **Key Case Studies:**
 
 
• **Sterlite Copper Plant Case:** The Supreme Court highlighted the importance of prior ECs when the plant was shut down due to environmental violations.
 
• **Western Ghats Mining Case:** Retrospective clearances were challenged, emphasizing the need for impact assessments before project approval.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ruling:**
 
 
• The decision ensures stricter compliance with environmental regulations, promoting **sustainable development**.
 
• It prevents industries from bypassing legal procedures, thereby safeguarding **environmental integrity**.

questions.question: In a landmark judgment on 8 April 2025, the Supreme Court deemed which state governor's refusal to assent to 10 state bills as illegal and unconstitutional?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **8 April 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** delivered a landmark judgment deeming the refusal of the **Tamil Nadu Governor** to assent to 10 state bills as **illegal and unconstitutional**.
 
• The judgment emphasized the **Governor's role** as a constitutional functionary and clarified that the Governor cannot act arbitrarily or delay assent without valid reasons.
 
• The court ruled that withholding assent for extended periods or rejecting bills passed by the **state legislature** violates the **federal structure** and the democratic principles enshrined in the **Constitution of India**.
 
• This decision set a precedent for addressing disputes related to the **Governor's discretionary powers**, reaffirming the importance of **accountability and timely decision-making** in constitutional governance.
 
• The judgment also underscored the principle that the Governor is bound by the advice of the **Council of Ministers** in most circumstances, as per **Article 163** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of the Governor in India:**

 
 
• The Governor is the **constitutional head of the state**, appointed by the **President of India**, and acts on the advice of the **Council of Ministers**.
 
• Under **Article 200**, the Governor can give assent, withhold assent, or reserve a bill for the consideration of the President.
 
• The Governor's discretion is limited, and decisions must align with the **constitutional framework**.
 
 
 
• **Article 200 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• **Article 200** governs the process of assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• The Governor can:
 
 
• Give assent to the bill,
 
• Withhold assent, or
 
• Reserve the bill for the President's consideration.
 
 
 
• The refusal to act on bills for extended periods is considered a violation of the **constitutional duty**.
 
 
 
• **Federal Structure of India:**
 
 
• India's governance system is based on a **quasi-federal structure**, where powers are divided between the **Union and the States**.
 
• Governors play a crucial role in preserving this balance but must adhere to the principles of **democracy and accountability**.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court as the Guardian of the Constitution:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to interpret the Constitution and adjudicate disputes between the **Union and State governments**.
 
• It ensures that the actions of constitutional authorities like Governors comply with the principles of **justice, equality, and democracy**.
 
 
 
• **Key Precedents:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has previously ruled on cases involving the discretionary powers of Governors, emphasizing their role as a **neutral constitutional authority**.
 
• Judgments like the **SR Bommai Case (1994)** have clarified the limitations on the Governor's powers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Governors and State Bills:**

 
 
• The Governor's role is primarily ceremonial, and decisions regarding state bills must reflect the advice of the elected government.
 
• Unnecessary delays or refusal to act on bills disrupt the **legislative process** and undermine the authority of state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Intervention:**
 
 
• Judicial review serves as a safeguard against arbitrary actions by constitutional functionaries.
 
• The Supreme Court's rulings ensure that the **Governor's powers** are exercised responsibly and in accordance with the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• Relevant articles include **Article 163** (Governor's discretion), **Article 200** (assent to bills), and **Article 201** (President's consideration).
 
• These provisions collectively define the framework for legislative processes at the state level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Judgment:**
 
 
• This judgment reinforces the principles of **democratic governance** and accountability.
 
• It ensures that Governors act within their constitutional limits, respecting the authority of elected governments.

questions.question: Which Indian state leads in mangrove afforestation under MISHTI scheme as of February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gujarat** leads in mangrove afforestation under the **Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)** scheme as of February 2025. The state has implemented extensive programs to restore and expand mangrove ecosystems along its coastline.
 
• The **MISHTI scheme**, announced in the **Union Budget 2023-24**, aims to promote mangrove conservation and restoration in collaboration with local communities and other stakeholders.
 
• Gujarat's success in afforestation is attributed to its vast **coastal area of about 1,600 km**, which includes regions like the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat, known for their suitable conditions for mangrove growth.
 
• Mangroves play a critical role in mitigating climate change by acting as **carbon sinks**, protecting shorelines from erosion, and supporting biodiversity. Gujarat has prioritized these aspects through its targeted afforestation efforts.
 
• Local communities in Gujarat are actively involved in the afforestation process under the MISHTI initiative, ensuring the sustainability of the restored mangrove ecosystems while also generating **livelihood opportunities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the MISHTI Scheme:**

 
 
• The **Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)** was introduced in the **Union Budget 2023-24** to restore mangrove ecosystems.
 
• It is implemented through **convergence** of schemes such as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) and Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA).
 
• The scheme focuses on mangrove plantation along India’s coastline and on saltpan lands, aiming to enhance biodiversity and climate resilience.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mangroves:**
 
 
• Mangroves are **salt-tolerant plants** that thrive in intertidal zones, serving as critical habitats for marine biodiversity.
 
• They act as effective **carbon sinks**, sequestering large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, thus mitigating climate change.
 
• Mangroves protect coastlines from **storm surges, erosion, and rising sea levels**, ensuring the safety of coastal communities.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat's Mangrove Restoration Efforts:**
 
 
• Gujarat has a **significant mangrove cover**, with the Gulf of Kutch being one of the largest mangrove ecosystems in the state.
 
• The state’s mangrove area has seen consistent growth due to focused afforestation initiatives and community participation.
 
• Gujarat has implemented various projects to restore degraded mangrove areas and expand mangrove cover along its coastline.
 
 
 
• **Other Leading States in Mangrove Conservation:**
 
 
• **West Bengal:** Home to the **Sundarbans**, the largest mangrove forest in the world, with significant biodiversity.
 
• **Odisha:** Known for its mangrove ecosystems in the Bhitarkanika region, which supports rich wildlife.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** Focuses on mangrove restoration in areas like the Godavari and Krishna delta regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India accounts for approximately **3% of the world’s mangrove cover**, with significant areas in states like Gujarat, West Bengal, and Odisha.
 
• The **State of Forest Report 2021** highlights that India’s mangrove cover has increased by **17 sq. km** compared to the previous assessment.
 
• Mangrove conservation is essential for achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly in combating climate change and promoting sustainable livelihoods.
 
• The Indian government has emphasized community participation in mangrove restoration, recognizing their importance in coastal ecosystem resilience.

questions.question: How many Kirti Chakras were conferred during the Defence Investiture Ceremony 2025 (Phase-I)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Defence Investiture Ceremony 2025 (Phase-I)**, a total of **4 Kirti Chakras** were conferred.
 
• The **Kirti Chakra** is India's second-highest peacetime gallantry award, given for acts of valor, courage, and self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
 
• The awardees of the Kirti Chakra typically include personnel from the **armed forces, paramilitary forces, and civilians** who have exhibited extraordinary bravery in challenging situations.
 
• The **Defence Investiture Ceremony** is an annual event where gallantry awards and other decorations are presented by the President of India to honor the recipients’ exceptional contributions.
 
• The correct number of Kirti Chakras awarded during this phase of the ceremony is officially documented and announced by the Ministry of Defence, ensuring transparency and recognition for the recipients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kirti Chakra:**

 
 
• The Kirti Chakra was established on **4 January 1952** as an award for gallantry during peacetime.
 
• It ranks **second after the Ashoka Chakra** but above the Shaurya Chakra in terms of peacetime gallantry awards.
 
• The decoration is awarded to both **military personnel and civilians** for their heroic deeds.
 
• Recipients of the Kirti Chakra are entitled to wear the medal and ribbon in ceremonial uniforms.
 
 
 
• **Defence Investiture Ceremony:**
 
 
• The Investiture Ceremony is conducted by the **President of India** at Rashtrapati Bhavan or another designated venue.
 
• Awards such as Kirti Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Shaurya Chakra, and other military honors are presented during this ceremony.
 
• The event acknowledges the **bravery, commitment, and sacrifices** of the recipients in the service of the nation.
 
• It serves as a platform for the nation to express gratitude to its heroes, both military and civilian.
 
 
 
• **Other Gallantry Awards:**
 
 
• **Ashoka Chakra:** India's highest peacetime gallantry award, given for exceptional courage and bravery.
 
• **Shaurya Chakra:** Awarded for distinguished service and gallantry during peacetime.
 
• These awards are typically conferred during **Republic Day** or **Independence Day** celebrations and ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The recipients are selected based on recommendations from their respective units or organizations.
 
• The nominations are reviewed by a panel of experts, ensuring that the awards are conferred to deserving individuals.
 
• The final list is approved by the **President of India** and announced publicly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Kirti Chakra is awarded for acts of valor performed during **peacetime operations**, including counter-terrorism, disaster relief, and rescue operations.
 
• The medal features a circular shape, with a depiction of **Ashoka's lions** and the words "Kirti Chakra" inscribed in Hindi and English.
 
• The ribbon accompanying the medal is **green with two orange stripes**, symbolizing courage and valor.
 
• Some of the notable recipients of the Kirti Chakra include individuals from the **Indian Army, Air Force, Navy, paramilitary forces, and civilians** who exhibited extraordinary bravery.

questions.question: Vaidya Tara Chand Sharma, Vaidya Maya Ram Uniyal and Vaidya Sameer Govind Jamadagni were the recipients of which of the following awards in 2025?

options.text: Nelson Mandela Award for Health Promotion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards** are prestigious awards given to individuals who have made significant contributions to the field of **Ayurveda** in India.
 
• Recipients of these awards are recognized for their dedication to promoting and preserving the ancient system of Ayurveda, which is a key component of India's traditional medical heritage.
 
• In the year **2025**, **Vaidya Tara Chand Sharma**, **Vaidya Maya Ram Uniyal**, and **Vaidya Sameer Govind Jamadagni** were honored with this award for their exceptional work in the field.
 
• The award is usually conferred by the **Ministry of AYUSH**, Government of India, which is responsible for promoting Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy.
 
• The recipients are often individuals who have contributed to **research, clinical practice, teaching, or the promotion of Ayurveda** at a national or international level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ayurveda:**

 
 
• Ayurveda is an ancient system of medicine that originated in **India over 5,000 years ago**.
 
• It is based on the principles of maintaining balance in the body through **diet, lifestyle, and natural remedies**.
 
• Ayurveda focuses on **holistic healing** and emphasizes the mind-body connection.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of AYUSH:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of AYUSH** (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy) was established in **2014** to promote traditional systems of medicine.
 
• It is responsible for the development, research, and education related to these systems of medicine.
 
 
 
• **National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards:**
 
 
• The award is named after **Dhanwantari**, the Hindu god of medicine and an avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is considered the father of Ayurveda.
 
• The award recognizes individuals who have made **outstanding contributions** to the research, innovation, and promotion of Ayurveda.
 
 
 
• **Other Awards in the Field of Medicine:**
 
 
• **National Florence Nightingale Awards:** These awards are conferred to outstanding **nurses and healthcare professionals**.
 
• **Nelson Mandela Award for Health Promotion:** This award recognizes contributions to **public health and health promotion** globally.
 
• **National Award to Teachers:** This award is given to educators for their **exceptional contributions to the field of education**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards:**

 
 
• Nominees must have demonstrated excellence in the practice, teaching, or research of Ayurveda.
 
• Their work should have a significant **impact on public health** or contribute to the advancement of Ayurveda.
 
 
 
• **Role of Ayurveda in Modern Healthcare:**
 
 
• Ayurveda is increasingly being integrated into modern healthcare systems, especially for **chronic diseases** and **preventive care**.
 
• Its emphasis on lifestyle and dietary practices aligns with modern concepts of **wellness and preventive medicine**.

questions.question: In May 2025, which of the following two companies received Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) in-principle approval for cross-border payment aggregation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PayPal and Worldline**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** granted **in-principle approval** for cross-border payment aggregation to **PayPal and Worldline** in May 2025, allowing these companies to facilitate payment processing for international transactions.
 
• **PayPal**, a global leader in digital payments headquartered in the **United States**, specializes in providing **secure and efficient cross-border payment services** for individuals and businesses worldwide.
 
• **Worldline**, a European company based in **France**, is a prominent payment service provider offering solutions for **e-commerce, international payment processing, and financial services**.
 
• Cross-border payment aggregation services are crucial for businesses engaged in international trade, as they allow for seamless **multi-currency processing, compliance with global regulations, and enhanced security measures**.
 
• By granting this approval, RBI aims to **strengthen India's digital payment ecosystem** and support the growing demand for international payment solutions in a rapidly globalizing economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PayPal:**

 
 
• Founded in **1998**, PayPal is an American multinational financial technology company headquartered in **San Jose, California**.
 
• It offers services including **online money transfers, currency exchange, and payment processing** for e-commerce platforms.
 
• PayPal supports over **200 markets** globally and allows transactions in **25 currencies**.
 
• The company focuses on providing **secure and user-friendly payment solutions** for businesses and individuals.
 
 
 
• **Worldline:**
 
 
• Worldline is a **French payment and transactional services company**, founded in **1974** and headquartered in **Bezons, France**.
 
• It is a leading provider of **international payment solutions**, offering services such as **merchant acquiring, digital payments, and terminal services**.
 
• The company operates in over **50 countries** and processes billions of transactions annually.
 
• Worldline specializes in **secure, scalable, and efficient payment systems** for enterprises and governments.
 
 
 
• **Cross-Border Payments:**
 
 
• Cross-border payments refer to transactions where the payer and the payee are located in different countries.
 
• These payments are vital for **international trade, e-commerce, remittances, and global supply chains**.
 
• They involve **currency exchange, compliance with international regulations, and anti-money laundering (AML) measures**.
 
• Technological advancements such as **blockchain** and **real-time payment systems** are driving innovation in the cross-border payment sector.
 
 
 
• **RBI’s Role in Payment Aggregation:**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India regulates payment aggregators to ensure **security, transparency, and compliance** in digital payment systems.
 
• RBI issues licenses to companies meeting stringent requirements, including **capital adequacy, technology infrastructure, and risk management**.
 
• It aims to promote **financial inclusion** and enhance the efficiency of India's payment ecosystem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options in the Question:**

 
 
• **PhonePe and Razorpay:** These companies are leading payment service providers in India but have not been granted in-principle approval for cross-border payment aggregation by RBI as of May 2025.
 
• **Amazon Pay and Instamojo:** While Amazon Pay is a significant player in digital payments, and Instamojo specializes in online payment solutions for small businesses, they do not hold RBI’s approval for cross-border payment aggregation.
 
• **Google Pay and Stripe:** Both companies are influential in the global payment ecosystem, but they have not received specific in-principle approval from RBI for cross-border payment aggregation.

questions.question: According to the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), which region was identified as the most polluted zone in India in October 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Gangetic Plain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indo-Gangetic Plain** was identified as the most polluted region in India in October 2025, according to a report by the **Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA)**.
 
• This region is one of the most densely populated areas in the world and spans across **northern and eastern India**, including states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab, Haryana, and West Bengal.
 
• The high pollution levels in the Indo-Gangetic Plain are primarily attributed to **stubble burning** during the harvest season, **vehicular emissions**, **industrial activities**, and **domestic fuel usage**.
 
• Seasonal factors like **winter smog** and low wind speeds exacerbate the problem, leading to a significant deterioration in air quality, often reaching hazardous levels.
 
• The region frequently records extremely high levels of **PM2.5** (fine particulate matter), which poses severe health risks, including respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plain:**

 
 
• This plain stretches from the **Indus River** in the west to the **Brahmaputra River** in the east.
 
• It is known for its fertile alluvial soil, making it a prominent agricultural hub in India.
 
• The plain is home to major cities such as **Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, and Kolkata**, which further contribute to the pollution due to urbanization and industrialization.
 
• Population density in this region is one of the highest globally, putting immense pressure on natural resources and air quality.
 
 
 
• **Factors Contributing to Pollution:**
 
 
• **Stubble Burning:** Farmers in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh burn agricultural residues after harvesting, releasing large amounts of pollutants.
 
• **Vehicular Emissions:** High vehicle density, especially in urban areas, leads to increased levels of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter.
 
• **Industrial Emissions:** Industries in the region, including thermal power plants, contribute significantly to air pollution.
 
• **Domestic Factors:** The use of solid fuels like wood and coal for cooking and heating in rural areas adds to pollution levels.
 
 
 
• **Health Impact of Pollution:**
 
 
• High levels of **PM2.5** and **PM10** particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and even enter the bloodstream, causing **respiratory and cardiovascular diseases**.
 
• Long-term exposure can lead to chronic diseases, reduced lung function, and premature deaths.
 
• Children and the elderly are particularly vulnerable to the health effects of air pollution.
 
 
 
• **Initiatives to Combat Pollution:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched initiatives like the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** to reduce particulate pollution by 20-30% by 2024.
 
• Programs like **Ujjwala Yojana** aim to reduce dependence on solid fuels by providing LPG connections to rural households.
 
• Efforts are also being made to promote cleaner technologies and stricter industrial emission norms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **PM2.5 and PM10:**

 
 
• **PM2.5:** Particulate matter with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers. These particles are small enough to enter the lungs and bloodstream, posing severe health risks.
 
• **PM10:** Particulate matter with a diameter of less than 10 micrometers, which can cause respiratory issues but does not penetrate as deeply as PM2.5.
 
 
 
• **Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA):**
 
 
• An independent research organization focused on analyzing the trends, causes, and solutions to air pollution and its impact on human health.
 
• CREA provides data-driven insights to support effective policymaking for cleaner air.
 
 
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **2019** by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
 
• Aims to reduce PM2.5 and PM10 levels in non-attainment cities by 20-30% by **2024** (compared to 2017 levels).
 
• Focuses on comprehensive planning, monitoring, and implementation of air quality improvement measures.

questions.question: With which defense organisation has the Indian Navy jointly conducted successful combat trials of the indigenously developed Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM) in May 2025?

__
 
• The **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** is the premier agency responsible for the research and development of defense technologies in India.
 
• In **May 2025**, the Indian Navy collaborated with DRDO to conduct successful combat trials of the **indigenously developed Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM)**.
 
• The **Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM)** is a state-of-the-art mine designed for maritime defense applications. It incorporates multiple sensors to detect and respond to various types of threats.
 
• The successful trials mark a significant milestone in India’s efforts to achieve **self-reliance** in defense technology under the government’s **‘Make in India’ initiative**.
 
• This achievement reflects the robust partnership between the Indian Navy and DRDO in enhancing India’s maritime security capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**

 
 
• Established in **1958**, DRDO operates under the Ministry of Defense, Government of India.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, DRDO oversees over **50 laboratories** dedicated to research in aeronautics, armaments, electronics, combat vehicles, engineering systems, and more.
 
• DRDO has been instrumental in developing technologies such as the **BrahMos missile**, **Agni series** of ballistic missiles, and **Akash surface-to-air missile systems**.
 
 
 
• **Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM):**
 
 
• This indigenously developed mine integrates multiple sensors, such as **magnetic, acoustic, and seismic sensors**, to detect various threats in marine environments.
 
• MIGM is designed for deployment on the seabed to target enemy ships and submarines effectively.
 
• It enhances operational flexibility and supports India’s maritime defense strategy by safeguarding critical sea routes and installations.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy’s Role in Defense Innovation:**
 
 
• The Indian Navy actively collaborates with DRDO and other defense organizations to develop advanced technologies for maritime security.
 
• Recent initiatives include the induction of platforms such as the **INS Vikrant** (India’s indigenous aircraft carrier) and advanced frigates and submarines.
 
• Such collaborations aim to reduce dependence on foreign imports and boost indigenous defense production.
 
 
 
• **‘Make in India’ Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in **2014**, the initiative aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub.
 
• The defense sector is a key focus area, promoting the indigenization of military hardware and technology.
 
• Under this initiative, defense organizations like DRDO have been encouraged to innovate and produce cutting-edge systems.

• Advanced radar systems, combat vehicles, and electronic warfare systems are among its notable contributions.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy’s Modernization:**
 
 
• The Indian Navy has consistently focused on modernizing its fleet with indigenous platforms, including **submarines, destroyers, and aircraft carriers**.
 
• The induction of sophisticated technologies like MIGM strengthens its capability to protect India’s maritime interests.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Maritime Defense:**
 
 
• India’s geographical location makes maritime security crucial for protecting trade routes and ensuring regional stability.
 
• Developments like MIGM enhance India’s ability to deter threats in its territorial waters and Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

• The theme of National Doctor’s Day in **2025** was **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__. This theme aimed to highlight the mental health challenges, emotional stress, and well-being of doctors, especially during the post-pandemic era.
 
• This theme brought attention to the need for providing support systems for **healthcare professionals**, who often experience **burnout, anxiety, and depression** due to their demanding roles.
 
• The global pandemic emphasized the critical role of doctors as front-line warriors, but it also revealed the emotional toll they endure while saving lives. The 2025 theme emphasized creating awareness and empathy for their struggles.
 
• Several healthcare organizations, governments, and institutions organized campaigns, seminars, and workshops on this day to address the importance of the **mental health of medical professionals**, ensuring their physical and emotional well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Significance of National Doctor’s Day:**

 
 
• Celebrated annually to recognize the services and contributions of doctors to society.
 
• It is a day to honor the role of medical professionals in improving health outcomes and saving lives.
 
• It also serves as a reminder of the importance of healthcare accessibility and medical advancements.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the 2025 Theme:**
 
 
• The theme **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__ shed light on the increasing cases of stress and mental health concerns among medical professionals.
 
• It highlighted the need for addressing issues like **workplace stress, long working hours, and lack of emotional support** in the healthcare industry.
 
• Organizations encouraged doctors to seek professional help and emphasized the importance of peer support and counseling programs.
 
 
 
• **Other Recent Themes:**
 __
 
• 2023: **"Celebrating Resilience and Healing Hands"** – Focused on honoring the relentless efforts of doctors during challenging times.
 
• 2024: **"Healing Hands, Caring Hearts"** – Highlighted the compassionate role of doctors in patient care.
 
• 2025: **"Behind the Mask: Who Heals the Healers?"**__ – Emphasized the emotional and mental well-being of doctors.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy:**
 __
 
• Born on **1 July 1882**, Dr. Roy was a celebrated physician, freedom fighter, and politician.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing medical institutions such as the **Indian Medical Association** and the **Medical Council of India.**
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian award, in **1961**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mental Health of Doctors:**

 
 
• Studies indicate that a significant percentage of doctors experience **burnout** due to the high-pressure nature of their profession.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** emphasizes the importance of providing mental health support and resources for healthcare workers.
 
• In India, initiatives like **helplines and counseling services** have been introduced to address these issues.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
